tools.name: addRelationship
tools.description: Add a relationship (Include/Extend/Generalization/Association) between elements in a use case diagram. Include: sourceName is the base use case, targetName the included one. Extend: sourceName is the extending (optional) use case and targetName the base use case the arrow points to. Generalization: sourceName is the child and targetName the parent (the hollow triangle is drawn at targetName). A relationship already joining the pair is reported, not drawn twice

tools.name: addSystemBoundary
tools.description: Wrap all use cases of a use case diagram in a labeled system boundary rectangle (the module box) and lay the diagram out around it: the box is sized to the use cases it holds, actors stand outside. A diagram has one boundary: calling it again renames it and adds the use cases added since.

tools.name: addUseCase
tools.description: Add a use case to a use case diagram. x/y (>0) place it explicitly (it stays there and the lines are routed around it); otherwise the layered layout places it

tools.name: addActor
tools.description: Add an actor to a use case diagram. x/y (>0) place it explicitly: it stays there and the lines are routed around it; otherwise the layered layout puts the actors in one column on the left (their names hang below the figures; a specialization of an actor is joined to its general actor by a bracket left of the column)

tools.name: generateUseCaseReport
tools.description: Generate a use case analysis report for a diagram

tools.name: createUseCaseDiagram
tools.description: Create a new use case diagram in Visual Paradigm

tools.name: addNote
tools.description: Add a note (a comment box with a folded corner) to any diagram, e.g. to explain a relation, a message or a state. attachedTo (the name of a shape on the diagram, "" = free-standing) joins it to that shape with a dashed anchor line. x/y (>0) place it; otherwise it goes at the first free spot beside the attached shape (right, left, below, above: overlapping no shape, label or line, and inside the lane of a shape in a swimlane), or below everything on the diagram. The text is broken into lines of about 30 characters and the box sized to it

tools.name: renameElement
tools.description: Rename the element a shape of a diagram shows (class, package, node, state, action, use case, actor, object, lifeline, table...): elementName is its current name on the diagram, newName the new one (unique on the diagram). Every diagram that shows the element follows; the shape is fitted to the new name. Not for connectors (re-add them) or ERD columns (renameColumn)

tools.name: autoLayoutDiagram
tools.description: Apply structured layout to a diagram. Call it after adding elements (every tool also lays the diagram out as it adds). Every diagram type except sequence and BPMN: layered, orthogonal layout of shapes, lines and labels: every line horizontal or vertical, no shape overlap, no line through a shape, no two lines on top of each other, labels beside their lines; shapes placed with x/y are not pinned any more. Class: generalizations decide the layers; UC: actors left, use cases inside the system boundary; state: initial at the top, final at the bottom, loops and opposite transitions side by side; activity: rows by the flow, nodes in the column of their lane, bars spanning their branches, page frames around their nodes; flowchart: top to bottom, a vertex of the decision per branch; communication: actor row, boundaries, controls, entities, message arrows beside their links. ERD: referenced tables left of the tables with their foreign keys. DFD: entities left, processes in the middle, data stores right. Component: layers and containers around their components, client above supplier, ports on the side their lines lead away to. Package: frames around what they hold, a package above the ones it depends on. Object: layers by the links. Deployment: nodes from left to right by their communication paths (stacked when that gives a rounder drawing), nested nodes, artifacts and components inside their node. BPMN: the auto-placed elements move left next to their sources and the pools narrow to their content (rows stay). Sequence diagrams are laid out as you add elements: nothing is moved (use setElementBounds and rerouteConnectors)

tools.name: listDiagrams
tools.description: List all diagrams in the project, optionally filtered by type: UseCase, Class, Sequence (= Interaction), Communication (= Collaboration), State (= StateMachine), Activity, Component, Deployment, Package, Object, ER (= ERD), BPMN, Flowchart, DFD, or the exact type shown in the list. The type is matched exactly, never as part of another name

tools.name: getElementCounts
tools.description: Get a summary of element types on a diagram (actors, use cases, classes, tables, etc.)

tools.name: getDiagramGeometry
tools.description: Dump the geometry of any diagram (the positions the add* tools answer with are the ones of that moment: the diagram is laid out again after every addition, this is the final picture): every shape with its bounds (nested shapes indented under their container, with the owner of a port) and every connector with its end shapes, its points, the bounds of its caption and the caption's text; a caption whose box is too small for Visual Paradigm to draw all of its text (it would end in "...") is marked TRUNCATED, with the size it needs. For checking a layout without a picture: connector ends, label positions, shapes inside their frame

tools.name: getDiagramElements
tools.description: Get all elements (shapes and connectors) on a diagram with their names, types, details and positions; connectors as 'Type <<stereotype>> name: from -> to [guard]'

tools.name: removeDiagramElement
tools.description: Remove an element (shape or connector) from a diagram by its model element name; a connector is also found by what getDiagramElements prints for it ("A -> B", "A -> B [guard]") and a message by its number ("5: tra ve"). A text that fits several connectors removes none and lists them. Only the view goes (with the connectors attached to a removed shape and the shapes nested in it); the model element stays in the project, except lifelines, links, messages, activity flows and state transitions, which exist on their diagram only

tools.name: addClass
tools.description: Add a class to a class diagram. x/y (>0) place the shape explicitly: it stays there and the connectors are routed around it; otherwise the layered layout places every class again as things are added (generalizations decide the layers, lines are horizontal or vertical, nothing overlaps). packageName draws the class inside that package frame (a package of that name already in the project is reused, the frame grows around its classes) and, for a new class, makes the package its owner. modelPackage puts the class inside a model package (no package shape drawn) so it cannot collide with same-named classes elsewhere in the project. A class of that name already in the project (root, or in modelPackage or the package) is reused: a new view of it is drawn

tools.name: addAttribute
tools.description: Add an attribute to a class. Type can be empty for analysis phase. When diagramName is given, only the class shown on that diagram is used (no project-wide fallback)

tools.name: removeAttribute
tools.description: Remove an attribute from a class shown on a class diagram (by name; every attribute of that name). The class box is fitted again. A wrong attribute is fixed with removeAttribute and addAttribute

tools.name: addPackage
tools.description: Add a package frame with an optional background color (#RRGGBB) to a class diagram. A package of that name already in the project is reused (a new view of it is drawn); a name already on the diagram is refused

tools.name: addDependency
tools.description: Add a dependency relationship between classes (dashed arrow)

tools.name: addOperation
tools.description: Add an operation/method to a class. params is 'name: Type, ...'. visibility is public/private/protected/package (empty = VP default). When diagramName is given, only the class shown on that diagram is used (no project-wide fallback)

tools.name: addAssociation
tools.description: Add an association between two classes in a class diagram

tools.name: addAggregation
tools.description: Add an aggregation relationship between classes (diamond open)

tools.name: removeOperation
tools.description: Remove an operation from a class shown on a class diagram (by name, whatever its parameters: every operation of that name). The class box is fitted again

tools.name: addComposition
tools.description: Add a composition relationship between classes (diamond filled)

tools.name: createClassDiagram
tools.description: Create a new class diagram in Visual Paradigm

tools.name: addRealization
tools.description: Add a realization (implements) relationship: fromClass implements the interface toClass (triangle on toClass)

tools.name: addGeneralization
tools.description: Add a generalization (inheritance): fromClass is the subclass (child), toClass the superclass (parent); the hollow triangle is drawn at toClass

tools.name: addInterface
tools.description: Add an interface to a class diagram (placed by the layered layout, like a class)

tools.name: addPackageShape
tools.description: Add a package frame at the given bounds. parentPackage (a package already on the diagram) nests it in that package, in the model and on the diagram; otherwise modelPackage (optional) is the model package that owns it. backgroundColor is '#RRGGBB' or empty

tools.name: addUsage
tools.description: Add a usage dependency (dashed arrow labelled <<use>>) from one class or package to another on a class diagram

tools.name: setClassColor
tools.description: Set background color of a class shape on a class diagram

tools.name: removeRelationship
tools.description: Delete relationships between two elements on a diagram from the MODEL (connector and model element). Class diagrams: relationshipType Generalization (fromClass = child, toClass = parent), Association (any kind), Aggregation, Composition, Dependency or Realization; associations match either direction. Every other diagram type (use case, activity, state, flowchart, DFD, BPMN, component, deployment, package...): fromClass and toClass are the names of the two shapes, relationshipType ("" or * = any) narrows by the kind of connector (Include, Extend, ControlFlow, Transition, BPSequenceFlow...), its stereotype or its label, and every connector between the two shapes in either direction that matches is removed (this is how an unnamed connector is deleted)

tools.name: getProjectInfo
tools.description: Name and file path of the project currently open in Visual Paradigm

tools.name: moveIntoPackage
tools.description: Put a class (or package) shown on a diagram into a package frame on the same diagram: the package becomes its owner in the model and its container on the diagram. Bounds are kept

tools.name: rerouteConnectors
tools.description: Route every connector of a diagram again around the shapes where they stand: every line is horizontal or vertical (right-angle elbows), clear of the other shapes, ends spread over the sides, labels beside the lines. Run after moving shapes; autoLayoutDiagram also moves the shapes

tools.name: exportDiagramImage
tools.description: Open a diagram and export it as an image to an absolute file path ending in .png, .jpg or .jpeg (a relative path would land inside Visual Paradigm's own folder)

tools.name: setElementBounds
tools.description: Move/resize a shape on a diagram. x or y <= 0 keeps the shape's current coordinate (a resize-only call is setElementBounds(name, 0, 0, w, h)); width or height <= 0 fits the shape to its content (a container such as a package, node or component keeps its size, and always stays big enough for what it holds). A container takes the shapes nested in it along (ports, artifacts, classes...); a lifeline of a sequence diagram takes its messages and activation bar along; control nodes, pseudo-states and BPMN/flowchart/DFD symbols keep their notation sizes. The labels of the connectors of a moved shape are routed again and their labels put beside the lines. A shape placed this way is pinned: the layered layout (class, use case, state, activity, flowchart, communication diagrams) leaves it where it is and routes the lines around it; a node of an activity swimlane stays in its lane (autoLayoutDiagram releases every pin)

tools.name: generateClassReport
tools.description: Generate a class diagram analysis report

tools.name: layoutConnectorLabels
tools.description: Put the labels of a diagram's connectors (multiplicities at the ends, names beside the longest leg) clear of shapes, lines and each other. The connectors are routed again around the shapes, which stay where they are

tools.name: getRelationshipDetails
tools.description: Audit dump (JSON) of a class diagram: classes (abstract, stereotypes, owner, attributes, bounds) and every relationship with both ends (multiplicity, aggregation kind, role) and name

tools.name: setAssociationProperties
tools.description: Update an existing association/aggregation/composition between two classes (either direction). fromMultiplicity/fromRole/fromNavigable apply to the end attached to fromClass. Empty values leave the property unchanged; role '-' clears the role name; navigable is true, false or unspecified

tools.name: addStereotypeToClasses
tools.description: Apply a stereotype (e.g. 'ORM Persistable') to classes on a diagram. classNames is a comma-separated list, or '*' for every class on the diagram. robustnessIcon true/false sets whether boundary/control/entity classes are drawn as robustness icons on this diagram (false keeps the class box with its members); empty leaves it unchanged

tools.name: newProject
tools.description: VP File > New Project: close the open project and start a new empty one (unsaved changes of the current project are discarded); save it with saveProjectAs

tools.name: saveProject
tools.description: Save the currently open project to its file

tools.name: openProject
tools.description: VP File > Open: open an existing .vpp file, replacing the open project (save it first; VP may ask about unsaved changes)

tools.name: saveProjectAs
tools.description: VP File > Save As: save the open project to a new .vpp path (parent folder must exist, existing files are not overwritten); the new file becomes the open project

tools.name: addColumn
tools.description: Add a column to a table shown on an ER diagram. columnType is a SQL type such as varchar, nvarchar(100), int, decimal(10,2), datetime; a length/scale written in the type wins over length/scale. Types the project's database does not know are mapped to their standard equivalent (nvarchar -> varchar, datetime -> timestamp, bit -> boolean, ...); a type that still cannot be set is reported as an error. varchar without a length gets 255. isUnique marks the column unique (the book's "U" next to the key). Names are SQL identifiers (no spaces or diacritics)

tools.name: removeColumn
tools.description: Delete a column of a table shown on an ER diagram (from the project, not just the view). A foreign key column cannot be removed: remove the foreign key first (removeForeignKey)

tools.name: createErd
tools.description: Create a new Entity-Relationship diagram in Visual Paradigm

tools.name: generateDdl
tools.description: Generate CREATE TABLE DDL statements for all tables in an ER diagram

tools.name: addForeignKey
tools.description: Add a foreign key: fromTable (the child) holds fromColumn, which references toColumn of toTable (the parent; empty toColumn = its primary key). The relationship is drawn with the crow's foot at the child. An existing fromColumn becomes the FK column; a fromColumn that does not exist yet is created with that name; when it is empty, Visual Paradigm adds a column named after the parent

tools.name: addTable
tools.description: Add a table/entity to an ER diagram. A table of that name elsewhere in the project is the same table and is shown again (with its columns). The layout puts the tables in columns by their foreign keys (referenced tables left) and every foreign key is a horizontal or vertical line; names are SQL identifiers (letters, digits, underscore: no spaces or diacritics)

tools.name: generateErdReport
tools.description: Generate an ERD analysis report

tools.name: removeTable
tools.description: Delete a table from the project (every diagram that shows it loses it). A table that is part of a foreign key is refused: remove the foreign keys first (removeForeignKey). removeDiagramElement removes only the view

tools.name: removeForeignKey
tools.description: Delete the foreign key between two tables shown on an ER diagram: parentTable is the referenced (one) side, childTable the table that holds the foreign key column. The foreign key column itself stays in the child (remove it with removeColumn)

tools.name: renameColumn
tools.description: Rename a column of a table shown on an ER diagram (a SQL identifier: letters, digits, underscores)

tools.name: addTableRelationship
tools.description: Add a relationship between tables (identifying or non-identifying): fromTable is the parent (referenced) table, toTable the child. fromMultiplicity is 1 or 0..1, toMultiplicity one of 0..1, 0..*, 1, 1..* ("" = 1 and 0..*)

tools.name: addActivation
tools.description: Add an activation bar to a lifeline in a sequence diagram

tools.name: addLifeline
tools.description: Add a lifeline (participant) to a sequence diagram. lifelineName is the head label and the handle used by addMessage (unique on the diagram). className is the classifier ("" = lifelineName; an existing class or actor of the project with that name is reused, never modified). lifelineType: actor | boundary | control | entity | participant or "" (plain box); boundary/control/entity draw the robustness icon for this lifeline only. An actor lifeline is drawn with a box head: Visual Paradigm does not draw a stick figure for a lifeline created through the API (its stick-figure actor cannot anchor messages)

tools.name: addReturnMessage
tools.description: Add a return message (dashed line, open head) between two lifelines in a sequence diagram; sequenceNumber as in addMessage

tools.name: addMessage
tools.description: Add a message between two lifelines in a sequence diagram. messageType: synch (default, solid line with a filled head), asynch (open head), create (the first message to a lifeline: dashed arrow ending at its head, which is lowered to the arrow) or destroy (the last message to a lifeline, which ends there with the X marker). sequenceNumber ("" = the next top-level number) is the number VP prints in front of messageName; a number already used on the diagram is refused. A label wider than the arrow moves the lifelines at its right apart

tools.name: generateSequenceReport
tools.description: Generate a sequence diagram analysis report

tools.name: addCombinedFragment
tools.description: Add a combined fragment frame (alt/opt/loop/break/par) to a sequence diagram. guard is the operand guard; separate several operands with '|' (e.g. "còn phòng|else" for alt/else). coveredLifelines is a comma list (empty = all lifelines). fromSeq/toSeq are the first and last top-level message numbers the frame encloses, nested ones (4.1, 4.2) included (0 = 1 / the last message); add the messages first. operandStarts is a comma list with the first top-level message number of operands 2..n (empty = share the messages out evenly). Messages are moved down to make room for the operator tab and guards, and the frame is widened to enclose the labels of the messages it covers

tools.name: createSequenceDiagram
tools.description: Create a new sequence diagram in Visual Paradigm

tools.name: createStateDiagram
tools.description: Create a new UML state machine diagram in Visual Paradigm. States auto-fit their text

tools.name: addFinalState
tools.description: Add a final state (bullseye) to a state machine diagram. stateName is the handle used by addTransition AND the label Visual Paradigm draws under the shape, so use a display-friendly name like "End". x/y (>0) place it explicitly

tools.name: addTransition
tools.description: Add a transition between two states of a state machine diagram. label is the UML text form 'event [guard] / effect' (pass "" for an unlabelled transition). Use the same state for fromState and toState to draw a self-transition (a rectangular loop on a free side). Every transition is a horizontal or vertical line; two opposite transitions between a pair of states run side by side. The diagram is laid out again after each transition (autoLayoutDiagram does it on demand)

tools.name: addState
tools.description: Add a named state to a state machine diagram. entryAction/doActivity/exitAction are optional behaviours shown in the state's compartment as 'entry / ...', 'do / ...', 'exit / ...' (pass "" to omit). The box is fitted to its text. x/y (>0) place the state explicitly (the transitions are routed around it), otherwise the layout puts it on the row its transitions lead to (the book's top-to-bottom screen flow, branches side by side)

tools.name: addInitialState
tools.description: Add the initial pseudo state (filled circle) to a state machine diagram. stateName is the handle used by addTransition AND the label Visual Paradigm draws under the circle, so use a display-friendly name like "Start". x/y (>0) place it explicitly

tools.name: addActivityFrame
tools.description: Add a rounded frame with a bold title at its top-left (a UML activity) to an activity diagram, the book's "Xử lí tại gdXxx.jsp" page frames. nodeNames is a comma list of the nodes the frame encloses: the layout keeps them together inside the frame (sized around them, with room for the title) and every other node outside it, so frames never overlap; call it after the nodes and their flows exist. With nodeNames "" the frame takes x/y/width/height. Calling it again with the same title changes the nodes of that frame. The frame stays behind the nodes

tools.name: addActivityAction
tools.description: Add an action (rounded box, fitted to its text) to an activity diagram. actionName is also the handle used by addActivityFlow, so it must be unique on the diagram; a trailing number ("Show #2") is only part of the handle, so the same text can stand in several page frames and the box shows "Show". partitionName puts it in that swimlane lane ("" = no lane). x/y (>0) place its top-left corner explicitly (kept inside the lane, the layout routes the flows around it); otherwise the layout puts it in the row its flows lead to, in the column of its lane

tools.name: addActivityFlow
tools.description: Connect two nodes of an activity diagram (by action/control/object node name) with a flow arrow. guard is the condition shown as [guard] on the arrow, typically on flows leaving a decision ("" = none; brackets optional). The flow is an object flow when either end is an object node, otherwise a control flow. twoWay=true also draws the flow back as a second arrow running beside the first (the book's action <-> "XxxDAO: method()" exchange). Every flow is a horizontal or vertical line (right-angle elbows); the branches of a decision leave from different vertices of its diamond, the inputs of a merge arrive on different sides, the flows of a fork or join meet the bar each at its own place. The diagram is laid out again after each flow: rows follow the flow, nodes stand in the column of their lane, nothing overlaps (autoLayoutDiagram does it on demand)

tools.name: addActivityControlNode
tools.description: Add a control node to an activity diagram. kind: initial | final | flowFinal | decision | merge | fork | join (fork/join are horizontal bars, decision/merge diamonds). nodeName is the handle used by addActivityFlow and must be unique on the diagram; a decision shows its question (e.g. "Valid?"), an initial or final node its name beside it ("Start"/"End"), the others none; a trailing number ("End #2") is only part of the handle, so a second final node or a second decision with the same text is added as "End #2" and shows "End"; a name that is only a number ("#1") makes a diamond with no text. partitionName puts it in that swimlane lane ("" = no lane). x/y (>0) place its top-left corner explicitly; otherwise the layout puts it in the row its flows lead to, in the column of its lane (a fork/join bar is as wide as the nodes it joins)

tools.name: createActivityDiagram
tools.description: Create a new UML activity diagram in Visual Paradigm. Shapes on it auto-fit their text

tools.name: addActivityPartition
tools.description: Add a vertical swimlane (partition) to an activity diagram. Lanes sit side by side in one swimlane frame: the first partition creates the frame at x/y (>0, otherwise 40,40), later ones are appended on the right and x/y are ignored. width/height (>0) size the lane body, otherwise 240x480 (wider for a long title); all lanes share the tallest height and grow automatically to enclose the nodes added to them with partitionName

tools.name: addActivityObjectNode
tools.description: Add an object node (rectangle, fitted to its text) to an activity diagram. state is shown under the name as [state] ("" = none). objectName is the handle used by addActivityFlow and must be unique on the diagram; flows to/from it are object flows. partitionName puts it in that swimlane lane ("" = no lane, or the lane under an explicit x/y). x/y (>0) place its top-left corner explicitly; otherwise the layout puts it in the row its flows lead to, in the column of its lane

tools.name: addComponent
tools.description: Add a component to a component diagram. stereotype is optional ("" = none, e.g. "subsystem"; several may be comma-separated; <<component>> is drawn by Visual Paradigm itself and ignored; a component that already exists in the project is reused and keeps its own stereotypes). parentComponent (a component already on the diagram, "" = none) nests the new component inside it, in the model and on the diagram, and the parent is sized around it. packageName (a layer frame added with addComponentPackage, "" = none) puts it in that package frame instead. x/y (>0) place the component explicitly in diagram coordinates and keep it there (the lines are routed around it), otherwise the layout decides: components in layers by their dependencies (the client above its supplier), inside their frame. The box is fitted to its text

tools.name: addPort
tools.description: Add a port (small square on the border) to a component of a component diagram. The layout puts a port on the side of its component its lines lead away to (its name outside), and the lines leave it outwards. A port can provide or require interfaces (addProvidedInterface / addRequiredInterface with the port name)

tools.name: addProvidedInterface
tools.description: Show that a component provides (realizes) an interface: a dashed realization with the hollow triangle at the <<interface>> box. componentName may also be a port added with addPort. Both must already be on the diagram

tools.name: addComponentPackage
tools.description: Add a package (layer) frame to a component diagram, e.g. "Presentation Layer", "Data Layer". Components added with packageName go inside it and the frame is sized around them. parentPackage ("" = none) nests it in another package frame. x/y (>0) place it explicitly and keep it there, otherwise the layout stacks the frames by the dependencies between their components (a layer above the layers it depends on); width/height (>0) size an explicitly placed frame (it still grows around its components). backgroundColor is '#RRGGBB' for a tint of its own ("" = the house blue, as the components in it). A package of that name already in the project (same owner) is reused

tools.name: addRequiredInterface
tools.description: Show that a component requires (uses) an interface: a dashed <<use>> arrow from the component to the <<interface>> box. componentName may also be a port added with addPort. Both must already be on the diagram

tools.name: createComponentDiagram
tools.description: Create a new UML component diagram in Visual Paradigm. Shapes added to it are fitted to their text

tools.name: addComponentDependency
tools.description: Add a dependency (dashed arrow) between two components, interfaces or ports of a component diagram. stereotype is optional ("" = none, e.g. "use", "call"; several may be comma-separated) and shown as <<stereotype>> on the arrow. Every line is horizontal or vertical; the diagram is laid out again after each dependency (autoLayoutDiagram does it on demand)

tools.name: addComponentInterface
tools.description: Add an interface to a component diagram, drawn as a box with the <<interface>> keyword (Visual Paradigm does not render its lollipop shape when it is created through the API). An interface of that name elsewhere in the project is reused. Connect it to components with addProvidedInterface (realization, hollow triangle at the interface) / addRequiredInterface (<<use>> dependency). x/y (>0) place it explicitly, otherwise the layout puts it between the component that requires it and the one that provides it

tools.name: addDeploymentNode
tools.description: Add a node to a deployment diagram. kind: node | device (<<device>>) | executionEnvironment (<<executionEnvironment>>); "" means node. parentNode ("" = top level) nests it inside a node already on the diagram, e.g. Tomcat (executionEnvironment) inside AppServer (device). x/y (>0, diagram coordinates) place it explicitly and keep it there, otherwise the layout decides (nodes from left to right by their communication paths, nested ones inside the parent). width/height (>0) are minimum sizes, otherwise the box is fitted to its caption; a node is sized around what is added into it and never smaller than the size asked for. A node of that name already in the project is drawn again with the kind it has. Node names must be unique on the diagram

tools.name: addDeploymentComponent
tools.description: Add a component hosted by a node of a deployment diagram (e.g. OrderService inside Tomcat): owned by the node and drawn inside it, auto-placed and fitted to its caption. nodeName may also name an artifact (View/Controller/Model inside app.war), which then encloses the component. nodeName "" draws it free-standing. Components of one host go in a row (left to right in the order added, 90 px apart, room for the label of the arrow between them) and the host grows to hold them; x/y (>0, diagram coordinates) place one explicitly. Component names must be unique on the diagram

tools.name: addDeploymentArtifact
tools.description: Add an artifact (e.g. app.war, schema.sql) to a deployment diagram. nodeName "" draws it free-standing (connect it with addDeployDependency); otherwise it is deployed into that node (owned by the node and drawn inside it), or drawn inside that artifact when nodeName names an artifact. x/y (>0, diagram coordinates) place it explicitly, otherwise it is auto-placed. The box is fitted to its caption. Artifact names must be unique on the diagram

tools.name: addDeploymentDependency
tools.description: Add a dependency (dashed open arrow) between two elements of a deployment diagram: components, artifacts or nodes, e.g. View -> Controller labelled "submit". label is shown on the arrow; "<<manifest>>" style text becomes a stereotype; "" leaves it unlabelled. Use addDeployDependency for artifact -> node deployments

tools.name: createDeploymentDiagram
tools.description: Create a new UML deployment diagram in Visual Paradigm

tools.name: addCommunicationPath
tools.description: Add a communication path (solid line) between two nodes of a deployment diagram. label is the protocol shown on the line, e.g. "HTTPS" or "JDBC"; write "<<TCP/IP>>" to show it as a stereotype instead; "" leaves it unlabelled

tools.name: addDeployDependency
tools.description: Add a <<deploy>> dependency (dashed arrow) from an artifact to the node it is deployed on. Use it for free-standing artifacts; an artifact drawn inside its node already shows the deployment

tools.name: addObject
tools.description: Add an object (instance specification) to an object diagram, rendered underlined as 'objectName : ClassName' with one compartment line per slot; objectName "" with a className draws an anonymous ': ClassName' object whose handle is the class name. className is looked up on this diagram, then in the project; if no class has that name a new class is created ("" = untyped object, no slots allowed). slots is 'attr=value;attr2=value2' ("" for none); each attr must be an attribute of the class or one of its superclasses (missing ones are added only to a class this call created). When several classes of the project carry that name (one per layer package), modelPackage names the package of the one to use; without it the class shown on this diagram, else the one that has all the slot attributes, is taken and the result names its owner. objectName is the handle used by addObjectLink. x/y (>0) place it explicitly and keep it there, otherwise the layout puts it in a layer by its links. The box is fitted to its content

tools.name: addPackageElement
tools.description: Add a package frame to a package diagram. parentPackage (a package already on the diagram, "" for none) nests it in that package, in the model and on the diagram; the parent is sized around it. x/y (>0, diagram coordinates) place it explicitly and keep it there (the lines are routed around it), otherwise the layout decides: packages in layers by their dependencies (a package above the ones it depends on), children inside their frame. width/height (>0) set the size of an explicitly placed frame; a frame is always at least 100x50, wide enough for its name and big enough for what it holds. backgroundColor is '#RRGGBB' for a tint of its own ("" = the house blue). A package of that name already in the project (root, or inside parentPackage) is reused: a new view of it is drawn

tools.name: addObjectLink
tools.description: Add a link (solid line) between two objects of an object diagram. label is shown on the line ("" for none). fromObject/toObject are object names on this diagram

tools.name: setObjectSlot
tools.description: Set, change or clear a slot of an object on an object diagram: attribute is an attribute of the object's class or of a superclass; value "" removes the slot. The box is fitted again. A wrong slot value is fixed with setObjectSlot instead of removing and re-adding the object

tools.name: addClassInPackage
tools.description: Show a small class box (name only, members hidden) inside a package frame of a package diagram. The class is owned by that package in the model: an existing class the package already owns is reused, otherwise a new class is created in the package. The box is fitted to its name, placed inside the package by the layout and the package is sized around it

tools.name: createPackageDiagram
tools.description: Create a new UML package diagram in Visual Paradigm

tools.name: addPackageDependency
tools.description: Add a dependency between two packages on a package diagram. kind is use|import|access|merge|line ("" = use): use draws a <<use>> usage (dashed open arrow), import/access/merge a dependency stereotyped <<import>>, <<access>> or <<merge>>, and line a plain solid line without arrowhead or keyword (the book's view - dao - model diagram). A class box shown in a package may also be used as an end

tools.name: createObjectDiagram
tools.description: Create a new UML object diagram in Visual Paradigm (slots are shown)

tools.name: addCommunicationLifeline
tools.description: Add a participant to a communication diagram. lifelineName is the label and the handle used by addCommunicationLink/addCommunicationMessage; leave it "" with a classifierName for an anonymous ':Classifier' object (the classifier name is then the handle). classifierName types an object box as 'name : Classifier' (an existing class of that name is reused; pass "" to show just the name). isActor=true draws a stick-figure actor instead (classifierName then links an existing use-case actor of that name, if any). lifelineType boundary | control | entity draws the object as that robustness icon (the book's GDxxx boundaries and entities; "" = plain box; the shared class is not modified). x/y (>0) place the shape explicitly, otherwise the diagram is laid out by its links (actor on top, then boundaries, controls, entities; every link a horizontal or vertical line). The shape is fitted to its text

tools.name: addCommunicationMessage
tools.description: Add a numbered message to a communication diagram, drawn as an arrow beside the link between the two participants (the link is created if missing); the arrow points fromLifeline -> toLifeline. sequenceNumber is the UML sequence expression such as "1", "1.2", "2a" or "1.1*"; pass "" to use one past the highest top-level number on the diagram. messageText is e.g. "validate()"; a leading "1.2:" in it is accepted and stripped because Visual Paradigm prints the number itself

tools.name: addCommunicationLink
tools.description: Connect two participants of a communication diagram with a link (the line messages travel along). Pass the same name twice for a self link. Reports the existing link instead of adding a duplicate

tools.name: moveCommunicationLifeline
tools.description: Move a participant (object, anonymous ':Classifier' object or actor) of a communication diagram to x/y (top-left corner). The participant stays there (autoLayoutDiagram releases it): its links are routed again with horizontal and vertical lines and the message arrows are laid out beside them

tools.name: createCommunicationDiagram
tools.description: Create a new UML communication (collaboration) diagram in Visual Paradigm. Message sequence numbers are shown and shapes are fitted to their text

tools.name: createFlowchart
tools.description: Create a new flowchart diagram in Visual Paradigm

tools.name: addFlowchartShape
tools.description: Add a symbol to a flowchart. kind is one of terminator (start/end oval), process, decision (diamond), inputOutput (parallelogram), document, predefinedProcess, database, manualInput, connector (on-page circle). shapeName is the text shown AND the handle used by addFlowchartFlow, so it must be unique on the diagram (a trailing number, "End #2", is only part of the handle: two terminators can both show "End"). The shape is fitted to its text; x/y (>0) set its top-left corner, otherwise it is placed by the layout: top to bottom, the branches of a decision side by side

tools.name: addDfdDataStore
tools.description: Add a data store to a data flow diagram. storeId is the label shown on the store ("D1" or "1": Visual Paradigm prints the D itself); pass "" to continue the diagram's numbering. The store can be referenced by name or ID in addDfdDataFlow. x/y (>0) set its top-left corner and keep it there, otherwise the layout puts it in the last column (right)

tools.name: addDfdDataFlow
tools.description: Add a data flow (arrow) between two elements of a data flow diagram, referenced by name or ID. label names the data moved, e.g. "order details" (pass "" for none). Every flow must start or end at a process; entity/store to entity/store flows are rejected. Every flow is a horizontal or vertical line; two opposite flows between a pair run side by side. The diagram is laid out again after each flow (autoLayoutDiagram does it on demand)

tools.name: addFlowchartFlow
tools.description: Connect two flowchart shapes with a flow line (arrow). label is shown on the line, e.g. "Yes"/"No" on decision branches (pass "" for none). Shapes are found by name on this flowchart; run rerouteConnectors after moving shapes

tools.name: addDfdProcess
tools.description: Add a process to a data flow diagram. processId is the number shown on the process (e.g. "1", "2", "1.0" or "1.1" on a child diagram); pass "" to continue the diagram's numbering (1.0 continues with 2.0). The process can be referenced by name or ID in addDfdDataFlow. x/y (>0) set its top-left corner and keep it there, otherwise the layout puts it between the entities (left) and the data stores (right)

tools.name: createDataFlowDiagram
tools.description: Create a new data flow diagram. notation: "" or standard (Visual Paradigm DFD: rounded process with ID, open-ended data store), ganeSarson, yourdonDeMarco (circle processes) or yourdonCoad. The add*Dfd* tools follow the diagram's notation automatically

tools.name: addDfdExternalEntity
tools.description: Add an external entity (source/sink outside the system, e.g. a customer or bank) to a data flow diagram. entityId is the marker shown in the corner of its box ("a", "b"...; "" continues the diagram's letters). x/y (>0) set its top-left corner and keep it there, otherwise the layout puts it in the first column (left)

tools.name: addBpmnDataObject
tools.description: Add a data object (document symbol, e.g. "Invoice" or "Order [approved]") to a BPMN diagram. Connect it to tasks or events with addBpmnSequenceFlow, which draws a data association (dotted arrow) for data objects. laneName is the lane (or a pool without lanes); "" puts it outside any pool. The name is drawn under the symbol and must be unique on the diagram. x/y (>0) set its top-left corner, otherwise it is placed under the last element of the lane

tools.name: addBpmnEvent
tools.description: Add an event (circle) to a BPMN diagram. position: start, intermediate or end. trigger: none (""), message, timer, error, signal, or terminate (end events only; end events cannot use timer). laneName is the lane (or a pool without lanes) it belongs to; "" puts it outside any pool. eventName is drawn under the circle AND is the handle used by the flow tools, so use a readable, unique name such as "Order received". x/y (>0) set its top-left corner, otherwise it is placed right of the last element of the lane, on the same row

tools.name: addBpmnTask
tools.description: Add an activity to a BPMN diagram. kind: task (plain), user, service, manual, send, receive, script, or subprocess (collapsed sub-process with a + marker); "" = task. laneName is the lane (or a pool without lanes) that performs it; "" puts it outside any pool. taskName is the text shown AND the handle used by the flow tools, so it must be unique on the diagram. The box is fitted to its text. x/y (>0) set its top-left corner (kept inside the lane), otherwise it is placed right of the last element of the lane, on the same row

tools.name: addBpmnPool
tools.description: Add a pool (participant, e.g. a company, department or external party) to a BPMN diagram as a horizontal band with its name on the left. x/y (>0) set its top-left corner, otherwise it is placed below the existing pools; width/height (>0) set its size, otherwise 900x160 (a height of 40-60 gives the thin band of a black-box participant that only receives and sends messages). The pool grows automatically to enclose its lanes and elements. Add lanes with addBpmnLane, or put elements directly in a pool without lanes

tools.name: addBpmnGateway
tools.description: Add a gateway (diamond) to a BPMN diagram. kind: exclusive (XOR, ""), parallel (AND), inclusive (OR) or eventBased. gatewayName is drawn above the diamond AND is the handle used by the flow tools; for a splitting gateway write the question, e.g. "In stock?", and label its outgoing flows with the condition parameter of addBpmnSequenceFlow. laneName is the lane (or a pool without lanes); "" puts it outside any pool. x/y (>0) set its top-left corner, otherwise it is placed right of the last element of the lane, on the same row

tools.name: addBpmnMessageFlow
tools.description: Connect elements of two different pools of a BPMN diagram with a message flow (dashed arrow with an open circle at the start), e.g. a customer task sending an order to the shop's start event. fromElement/toElement are task, sub-process, event or pool names (a pool stands for a black-box participant). label names the message, e.g. "Order" (pass "" for none). Start events can only receive and end events only send; gateways, lanes and data objects cannot take message flows

tools.name: addBpmnLane
tools.description: Add a lane (role or department inside a participant) to a pool of a BPMN diagram. Lanes are stacked top to bottom in the order they are added: the first lane fills the pool, each further lane is added below it and the pool grows. Add all lanes of a pool before putting elements into it

tools.name: createBpmnDiagram
tools.description: Create a new BPMN 2.0 business process diagram in Visual Paradigm

tools.name: addBpmnSequenceFlow
tools.description: Connect two elements of the same pool of a BPMN diagram with a sequence flow (solid arrow), referenced by name. A target that was auto-placed and has no incoming flow yet moves right of its source (on the source's row in the same lane, the next row down for a gateway's further branches, the source's column offset in another lane). condition labels the flow, e.g. "Yes"/"No" or "[in stock]" on the branches of a gateway (pass "" for none). BPMN rules are checked: no flow out of an end event, none into a start event, none across pools (use addBpmnMessageFlow). If one end is a data object a data association (dotted arrow) is drawn instead
